text:
Alex W: heads-up — ran a focused apples-to-apples across dedicated pool with both synthetic client and replay harness. found a weird delta on scale-up latency when kv cache is cold.
Maria G: how big is the delta? numbers pls.
Alex W: synthetic 99p scale-up to target GPUs ~2.2s, replay harness ~3.8s median. failure rate small but 2x tail.
Jin K: i profiled the runtime during the replay run. kernel selector spends more time evaluating blocksize heuristics because replay workloads have longer average seq len (80 vs synth 32). selecting an unfriendly kernel leads to extra memcpy and slower init.
Samir: are we warming KV cache the same way? replay doesn't preserve client-side prefix cache so first-reqs are touching kv-store hotpath.
Alex W: correct — replay runs real traces without prefix warmup. i added a warmup toggle and results changed: with kv-warmup, replay 99p drops to ~2.4s.
Jin K: attached profiler snippet (summarized):
```
runtime.selectKernel()  ->  48% time (replay cold)
kv.fetchPrefixes()    ->  22% time
gpu_memcpy            ->  12% time
other                 ->  18%
```
Maria G: ok that's helpful. sounds like 2 orthogonal issues: (1) kernel selection overhead for unexpected seq distribution, (2) kv cold hits adding +IO.
Samir: i also saw burst-credit accounting behaving oddly during the replay bursts — credits get depleted quicker and then scale-up pauses waiting for credits to replenish, prolonging the visible tail.
Alex W: repro steps i used: run bench harness:
```
# replay harness
./replay_runner --trace=prod_2025-03-12.json --concurrency=80 --target-pool=dedicated-g4x --warmup=false

# synthetic
./synth_driver --qps=1200 --seq-mean=32 --target-pool=dedicated-g4x
```
bench-bot: benchmark finished. summary (cold-warmup disabled):
```
synthetic: scale_time_99p = 2.2s, error_rate=0.1%
replay:    scale_time_99p = 3.8s, error_rate=0.4%
replay+kvwarm: scale_time_99p = 2.4s, error_rate=0.12%
```
Jin K: one proposed fix: cache the kernel decision per model+seq-bucket for the first N minutes so selector isn't recomputing expensive heuristics on each cold-run. cheap to implement and lowers selector cost by ~40% in my microbench.
Maria G: risk is mischoosing kernel for edge sequences, but we can add fallback to dynamic reselect after first chunk. sound ok?
Samir: for the burst credits, we should treat dedicated pools differently: allow temporary overdraft for scale-up path when autoscaler is triggered by traffic spike from replay-like bursts.
Alex W: agreed. action items:
- Jin: prototype kernel-decision cache + microbench (ETA 3d)
- Samir: run credit-policy sim with overdraft flag (ETA 2d)
- Maria: add a replay warmup step to CI harness and a synthetic vs replay comparison test (ETA 1d)
- Alex: capture full perf traces for next meeting (i'll upload to s3)

Maria G: also can we add a small test that toggles quantization path? replay seems to bias toward longer sequences which hits a non-quant path more often and may influence kernel selection.
Jin K: good call. i'll include quant-path flag in the prototype.
Samir: FYI oncall-bot just flagged a customer incident where dedicated pool saw a 30% tail increase during a marketing-triggered replay burst. might be same root cause.
oncall-bot: Incident #INC-2025-034 assigned to eng-runtime oncall.
Alex W: thanks — i'll correlate traces. any objections to locking this to a short spike remediation (kernel cache + kv warmup in the rollout)?
Maria G: no objections. please keep rollout behind a feature flag. :+1:
Jin K: noted. i'll PR the kernel cache and add tests comparing synth vs replay.
Samir: i'll update the autoscaler simulation and ping infra for dedicated-pool credit policy review.
Alex W: cool — next sync in 48h. cheers. :rocket:
